intro: Imputation can leak heldout information when statistics are fitted on all data. Explicit missingness masks let you fit medians on training observations only.
task: Fit medians on observed training entries, then transform heldout values without letting heldout extremes affect the fitted statistics.
requirements: train and values are finite numeric matrices with equal positive feature counts; train has at least one row. Each missing mask must be a boolean NumPy array of the corresponding matrix shape.
Fit each feature median using only train entries whose train_missing mask is false. Reject a feature with no observed training values.
Return dict medians as a feature vector and filled as a copy of values with value_missing entries replaced. Masked numeric placeholders do not affect fitted medians.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Heldout extremes do not change median

hints.title: Ignore placeholders during fitting
hints.body: Index each training column with the inverse of its missingness mask.

hints.title: Broadcast fitted statistics
hints.body: A feature median vector can fill matching columns without reading heldout statistics.

explanation: Fit and transform are distinct operations. The feature statistics depend only on observed training entries, and the transform reuses those statistics on any aligned matrix.
A separate boolean mask avoids overloading a numeric sentinel such as zero or NaN. Zero can be a valid observation, and arbitrary masked placeholders must not influence the median.
